parts.latex:
The probability that a new variety of seed will produce flowers in the first year of growth after being planted is 0.4. There were 200 seeds of this new variety planted.

How many of the seeds would be the expected frequency to NOT produce flowers in the first year ?

solutions.latex:
$$P(\text{not flowers}) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected number} &= 0.6\times 200 \\ &= 120 \end{aligned}$$

So $120$ seeds are expected not to produce flowers.

Two of the three equal sections are unshaded, so the probability of landing on an unshaded part is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected number} &= \dfrac{2}{3}\times 450 \\ &= 300 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Three unbiased six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously 1080 times.

How many times would it be expected that all three dice show a 4?

solutions.latex:
The probability that all three dice show a 4 is
$$\dfrac{1}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{1}{216}$$
Expected number of times:
$$\dfrac{1}{216}\times 1080=5$$
criteria: Finds the probability $\dfrac{1}{216}$, or equivalent merit

Elise plays a game using the spinners with the following 3 financial outcomes.

\begin{itemize}
\item Win \$12 for a score of 4
\item Win nothing for a score of less than 4
\item Lose \$3 for a score of more than 4
\item It costs \$5 to play this game.
\end{itemize}

Will Elise expect a gain or a loss and how much will it be?

Justify your answer with suitable calculation

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Wrote the conditional notation for clarity; the source gave only the value.

solutions.latex:
Expected return is the sum of each outcome's value times its probability, less the cost to play.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected return} &= \dfrac{1}{3}\times12+\dfrac{1}{2}\times0-\dfrac{1}{6}\times3-5 \\ &= -1.5 \end{aligned}$$

Elise should expect to lose $\$1.50$ on average.
criteria: Calculates the expected return with one error, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
There are $36$ equally likely outcomes in the array. Count the sums of $10$ or more.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{sum } 10 &: 3 \text{ ways} \\ \text{sum } 11 &: 2 \text{ ways} \\ \text{sum } 12 &: 1 \text{ way} \end{aligned}$$
This gives $6$ outcomes, so $P(\text{sum}\ge 10)=\dfrac{6}{36}=\dfrac{1}{6}$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected frequency} &= 500\times\dfrac{1}{6} \\ &\approx 83 \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

parts.latex:
Three unbiased six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously $1080$ times.

How many times would it be expected that all three dice show a $4$?

solutions.latex:
The three dice are independent, so multiply the probabilities.

$$P(\text{triple }4)=\dfrac16\times\dfrac16\times\dfrac16=\dfrac{1}{216}$$

The expected number of times is the probability times the number of rolls.

$$\text{expected number}=\dfrac{1}{216}\times1080=5\text{ times}$$
criteria: Finds the probability of triple 4, or equivalent merit
